points.point: The Vault's only linkage of signal generators to an AI-related application domain is the high-speed digital/AI-server deck, where signal generators are mapped to RefClk and PLL jitter performance alongside phase noise analyzers.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: replaces RefClk/PLL jitter mapping with Digital I/Q/interconnect claims

points.point: The same source maps signal generators to ADC/DAC frontend performance testing, together with spectrum analyzers.
points.label: missing
points.why: no ADC/DAC frontend performance or spectrum analyzer mapping

points.point: That instrument mapping comes with no test conditions, and the Vault forbids converting these instrument categories into formal product configurations or capability claims.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: states capability/spec claims despite reference saying no conditions or formal claims

points.point: The AI context of that high-speed digital source is the Taiwan AI server eco-chain, i.e. AI data-center/server hardware, not AI algorithm testing.
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions AI data center/server hardware, but not Taiwan eco-chain or distinction from algorithm testing

points.point: The Vault's AI/ML wireless use case is AI-enhanced CSI feedback using a two-sided AI model to compress and report channel state information — a modem/algorithm topic, not a signal generation capability.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: treats cellular/wireless RF generation as an AI signal-generation capability

points.point: In that AI demonstration the test instrument is the R&S CMX500 configured as an AI-enabled base station emulator, not a vector signal generator.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: points to vector signal generation instead of CMX500 base-station emulator

points.point: Where the Vault does list concrete signal generation capabilities (SMW200A: LTE, Cellular IoT, 5G NR R17/18 K171, OFDM K114, custom digital modulation), the stated application is 3GPP NTN component testing, not AI.
points.label: contradicted
points.why: attributes cellular/4G/5G signal-generation capabilities to AI rather than NTN

invented: High-speed digital / AI data center interconnect: Support high-speed digital input connectivity aligned with the R&S Digital I/Q Interface
Server, storage, and data center architectures: Preserve signal integrity, reliable data transmission, and scalable performance
Cellular / wireless connectivity: Generate RF signals for data-intensive cellular connectivity applications
4G/5G wireless testing: Use vector signal generation with high output power, wide modulation bandwidth, and excellent signal quality
4G/5G wireless bands: 8 kHz to 6 GHz frequency range
4G/5G modulation stress: up to 1 GHz RF modulation bandwidth
Radar / sensing: Generate complex pulsed signals using wide bandwidth
main signal-generation requirements are wideband, high-quality vector RF generation; high-speed digital I/Q connectivity
